🎤 AIChE Annual Conference Presentation # 7

 Our last talk at AIChE 2026 is from Max Bloor!

📌 Talk: Addressing Terminal Constraints in Reinforcement Learning-Based Demand Response Scheduling

👥 Authors: Max Bloor (presenting), Martha White, Calvin Tsay, Ehecatl Antonio del Rio Chanona
 
Electrified chemical plants can save money by shifting their load in time with respect to electricity prices however, the stored product has to be at a safe level for the following scheduling period. This creates a sparse learning problem for data-driven algorithms, such as RL, since the storage penalty is only at the end of a horizon that can be 72 hours long. Max will show how Goal-Space Planning splits that horizon into storage-level subgoals, which propagates information on how early decisions effected the terminal constraint satisfaction. On an air separation unit benchmark, it matches the savings of vanilla RL approaches with significantly fewer training episodes.

Preprint (IFAC World Congress 2026): https://lnkd.in/er7PdAkb
Earlier work, Hierarchical RL-MPC (DYCOPS 2025): https://lnkd.in/eatQXzDF

🎤 AIChE Annual Conference Presentation # 6

Our next AIChE talk will be given by Max Bloor!

📌 Talk: Non-Parametric Q-Learning for Process Systems Engineering

👥 Authors: Max Bloor (presenting), Max Mowbray, Ehecatl Antonio del Rio Chanona, Calvin Tsay

Self-driving labs and automated bioprocess platforms must learn a controller from tens to hundreds of experiments, each one expensive. Deep RL typically needs thousands of episodes, and tuning it costs even more experiments. Max will present Heteroscedastic Gaussian Process Q-learning (HGPQ), which learns the Q-function directly with a Gaussian process and needs no tuned learning rate. Each update is trusted according to how well the next time step's GP uncertainty estimate, and the value estimate provably converges to the optimal Q-function over the explored region. The algorithm is tested over a range of chemical, biological and classical control tasks which show improvements in sample efficiency over previous GP Q-learning and deep RL techniques.
 
Come along if you work on control or experimentation where every run counts!

Earlier GPQL paper (RLC 2025): https://lnkd.in/eiVPZaWX

🎤 AIChE Annual Conference Presentation # 5

Our next AIChE talk will be given by Matthew Marsh 🏑 🧠 
 
📌 Talk: Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification In Constrained Neural Networks for Model Predictive Control

👥 Authors: Matthew Marsh, Benoit Chachuat, Ehecatl Antonio del Rio Chanona

How can we ensure neural network models are physically consistent and provide reliable uncertainty estimates for safe process control?

In this talk, we combine differentiable constraint projection layers with conformal prediction to guarantee satisfaction of known physical relationships while providing distribution-free uncertainty quantification. We demonstrate how these properties can be exploited within nonlinear model predictive control to improve reliability under noisy data and process disturbances.

🎤 AIChE Annual Conference Presentation # 4

Our next AIChE talk will be given by Emma Pajak!

📌 Talk: Sketch2Simulation: Automating Flowsheet Generation Via Multi-Agent Large Language Models

Authors: Abdullah Bahamdan, Emma Pajak, Rohit Patwardhan, Kalpesh Patel, John Hedengren, Ehecatl Antonio del Rio Chanona

Converting process diagrams into executable simulation models traditionally requires substantial manual effort and simulator-specific expertise. 

Sketch2Simulation introduces an end-to-end multi-agent LLM framework that automates this process, translating raw engineering diagrams directly into Aspen HYSYS flowsheets. Combining diagram interpretation, simulation model generation and multi-level validation, the framework demonstrates the potential of multi-agent AI to automate complex process engineering workflows.
 
Join us to learn how multi-agent LLMs can automate the gap between process flow diagrams and flowsheet simulation models.
 
📄 Read it on arXiv: https://lnkd.in/eTmC6rdW

📌 Talk: Human-In-the-Loop Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Robust and Constraint-Aware Bioprocess Development

👥 Authors: Samuel Stricker, Lucas Francisco dos Santos, Claus Wirnsperger, Alessandro Butte, Laura Marie Helleckes, Gonzalo Guillen Gosalbez, Ehecatl Antonio del Rio Chanona, Mehmet Mercangöz

🧪 Bayesian Optimization can cut the number of experiments needed in bioprocess development, but a black-box algorithm that can’t take expert knowledge on board is hard to trust in a regulated, quality-by-design setting. 

🧑‍🔬 Come see how Pareto Front Guided Sampling puts the scientist back in control by laying out the trade-offs between titer, uncertainty, constraint satisfaction, and robustness, so experts can steer each round of experiments with their process knowledge. 🧠

🎉 Welcome to the new academic year!

At OptiML PSE, we’ve kicked off the year with our first group meeting and a group Hackathon at the Imperial College London White City Campus!

This year, we had the pleasure of welcoming back Isabela Fons to host the hackathon. We split into teams and competed to learn the best #ReinforcementLearning policy for residential energy management, with the goal to minimise energy costs, maintain a comfortable indoor temperature, and ensure sufficient battery charge for EV trips. ⚡🏡🚗

Congratulations to our hackathon winners Daniel Crîstiu, Max Bloor, Ammar Ali, and Yukang Wu! 🏆

Beyond the hackathon, we also had the chance to get to know each other better and explore topics beyond our #MachineLearning and #ProcessSystemsEngineering expertise through a spot quiz organised by Emma Pajak.

Here’s to another year of research, learning, and collaboration!

Niki’s PhD focused on multi-agent reinforcement learning for decision making under uncertainty. Many thanks to her PhD examiners, Prof. Michel-Alexandre Cardin and Prof. Alexandra Brintrup, for an excellent viva and scientific discussion.

It has been a real pleasure having Niki in the group and seeing her research develop over the course of her PhD and holding up the multi-agent reinforcement learning frontier! We are also very excited to see what comes next: Niki is now Co-Founder of Lamb Labs (YC S26), where she is working on custom chips for the fastest AI inference at the lowest power. 🚀

🧠 Talk: Addressing Terminal Constraints in Data-Driven Demand Response Scheduling

As chemical processes become increasingly electrified, there are growing opportunities to operate flexibly in response to changing electricity prices. However, ensuring systems end in a safe and stable operating state remains a major challenge for data-driven control. ⚡🏭

In this work, Max combines reinforcement learning with goal-space planning to enable long-horizon scheduling that satisfies critical terminal constraints while improving learning efficiency. Demonstrated on an air separation benchmark, the approach significantly outperforms conventional reinforcement learning methods, producing more reliable and less myopic control policies. 🤖📈

Analysts are coining it the Super Wednesday for supply chain research at IFAC! 🔗🚀 Alongside Lavinia, Daniel Crîstiu will be showcasing his work on designing economically viable supply chains for Carbon Capture and Utilization (CCU). 🌱

🧠 Talk: Market Mechanisms Assessment for Carbon Capture and Utilization: Optimal Supply Chain Design for Green Olefin Production

CCU offers a promising route to decarbonising the chemical industry, but can it actually compete economically with conventional fossil-based production? 🌍💰

In this work, Daniel develops an optimal CCU supply chain, converting biogenic CO₂ → alcohols → green olefins, and investigates how carbon pricing, hydrogen subsidies and product credits can help close the gap with fossil-based alternatives. 🏭♻️

The results show that green olefins remain uncompetitive under current UK market conditions; but that the right combination of market mechanisms can change the picture, providing a quantitative framework for policy-aware decisions around future CCU deployment. 📊🌱

🧠Mixed-Integer Programming for Optimal Reconfiguration of Supply Chains

Supply chains are increasingly exposed to structural changes driven by the energy transition and other external disruptions. In this work, she has developed a mixed-integer programming framework for optimally reconfiguring supply chains, helping preserve industrial operations and profitability as these networks evolve. 🔗📈

By combining product and spatial information to intelligently restrict the search space, the approach can rapidly identify high-quality solutions and explore alternative reconfiguration scenarios. The framework is demonstrated on an agricultural waste supply chain. 🌱♻️

We’re kicking off our IFAC World Congress 2026 showcases with Matthew Marsh 🚀

🧠 Talk: Embedding Linear Equality Constraints in Probabilistic Neural Networks for Dynamic Modelling

Modern data-driven models often have no knowledge of underlying physical laws, and in many cases provide deterministic estimates. In this work, we present a probabilistic modelling framework that embeds known physics as linear equalities directly into the model. This enables predictions that are guaranteed to be physically consistent, whilst providing calibrated uncertainty estimates and remaining robust under noisy data and constraints🤖📈

Happy to share that our latest work on computer-aided synthesis planning ("From Feasible to Practical: Pareto-Optimal Synthesis Planning") got accepted (spotlight) at [ICML] Int'l Conference on Machine Learning 🇰🇷.

📌 In molecular discovery, two critical stages often get treated separately: discovering synthesis routes for a target molecule (retrosynthesis) and optimizing those routes for the practical objectives that actually matter in industry. In this work, we bring them together. By directly embedding multiple real-life objectives into the search, we uncover Pareto optimal synthesis routes that capture the trade-offs between objectives; finding routes overlooked by traditional algorithms while also producing more diverse solutions.

Small technical TL;DR: we achieve this via weight-scalarized A* planning and BO-informed weight-sampling. We also provide a theoretical guarantee under which our algorithm is certified to return the complete Pareto front for the search space. 

The paper and code repo are below. You can run the algorithm yourself and define your own objectives. Contributions are welcome; there's definitely still a lot more exciting research to do!

I was glad to be at the [AISTATS] International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics in Tangier a couple of weeks ago, which was my first conference in my PhD.

I enjoyed presenting our work, "Learning with Embedded Linear Equality Constraints via Variational Bayesian Inference" at the OPTIMAL workshop.

Often, within real-world systems, we have physical domain knowledge that we want our models to satisfy. However, due to noise, often within the data, constraints do not hold exactly. We explore how to handle this through probabilistic projections that enforce constraints at all times, whilst both quantifying predictive uncertainty and retaining flexibility in the learned dynamics.

It was a great experience meeting different researchers within the community, and hearing about lots of exciting work in the area.

Thanks to my supervisors, Ehecatl Antonio del Rio Chanona and Benoit Chachuat for their guidance in putting this work together, and if you are interested, check out our preprint:

Excited to share our latest work, “MolPrice: assessing synthetic accessibility of molecules based on market value”, recently published in the Journal of Chemoinformatics and led by Friedrich Hastedt.

In this study, we introduce a machine learning framework that predicts the market price of organic molecules. Using self-supervised contrastive learning, we show that predicted price serves as an effective proxy for synthetic accessibility (SA), a key consideration in molecular discovery workflows. With NumPy-accelerated batching, MolPrice achieves prediction times below 0.1 ms per molecule, making it highly suitable for large-scale screening.

We further demonstrate how MolPrice can streamline virtual screening workflows by prioritizing molecules that are either easier to synthesize or directly purchasable from suppliers such as MolPort or Mcule. When a high-potential molecule is already available on the market, chemists can bypass time-consuming synthesis steps and proceed directly to experimental validation.

If you work in the field of molecular discovery and would like to explore MolPrice, the paper and the open-source code are available below:
